key_insight: A 5-qubit superconducting processor demonstrated end-to-end quantum training and testing for beauty-versus-charm jet identification without significant performance degradation from hardware noise.
engineering_relevance: The work demonstrates a real-hardware classification workflow and proposes a framework for estimating training time and optimizing circuits on resource-limited quantum processors.
method: Classify simulated LHCb beauty and charm jets using a variational quantum circuit.
Perform both training and testing on an IQM 5-qubit superconducting processor at Politecnico di Torino.
Evaluate hardware-noise effects and develop a training-time and circuit-optimization framework.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on simulated LHCb collision data found that hardware-induced quantum noise did not significantly degrade classification performance; the abstract provides no numerical metrics.
watch_item: Quantum advantage remains unproven, and scaling to high-dimensional jet data on larger devices requires further investigation.
paper_title: Beauty and charm jet identification with end-to-end training on a superconducting quantum processor
